home.lead: Quijote is a small, parent-run playgroup for 14 children aged 18 months to 6 years. Our caregivers are native Spanish speakers, so children grow up with two languages as a natural part of every day.
home.heroAlt: Group room wall: gelb – amarillo, rot – rojo (yellow, red)

pillars.p: In morning circle, in songs, at the table: Spanish and German are everyday languages here. Children learn through play, and German gets focused support for a smooth start at school.
14 children, three permanent caregivers, always two in the room. Older and younger children learn from each other in a mixed-age group.
Quijote is a parents' association. We cook once a week, meet regularly and shape the group together with the team.

concept.h1: Childhood is a life stage of its own – and of equal value.
concept.lead: We follow the situational approach and the Vienna Education Plan. Every child is supported in their individuality and creativity – with respect, warmth and without authoritarian rules.

blocks.p: Children are active, creative people. We take their feelings, ideas, fears, wishes and questions seriously, talk them through and offer ways to work through them.
We speak with the children in both languages. Songs, rhymes, finger games and books build vocabulary in Spanish and German. Two years before school we start observing language development closely.
In play, children discover what they can do. We hold back, observe carefully and keep re-arranging rooms and materials around what we see.
We guide everyday conflicts openly and look for solutions that are fair to both sides – the basis for a strong, balanced self-confidence.
Every day we head to nearby Rubenspark. Add dance, music, weekly yoga and monthly trips to museums, theatre or the zoo.
Our cook prepares fresh meals four days a week; on the fifth, parents cook. Wholesome, organic food, plus a weekly organic fruit and veg box.
We follow the Berlin settling-in model: step by step, together with a familiar parent or carer.
In the last year before school there is a pre-school programme every Wednesday with stories, experiments, pre-writing exercises and movement games.
Quijote has no religious affiliation. We celebrate St Martin, St Nicholas or Easter as traditions – with respect for every family.

faq.lead: The key answers at a glance. Didn't find yours? Just write to us.

items.a: Children from 18 months to 6 years, in one mixed-age group of up to 14 children.
Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:00. We close around Christmas and Easter; families receive the exact calendar directly.

items.q: Does my child need to speak Spanish?
items.a: No. Most children come from bilingual families, but Spanish isn't a requirement. Children pick it up through play – and German gets focused support.
Quijote is a parents' association: parents make decisions together, cook once a week and help with celebrations and outings.
Children bring a morning snack from home (no sweets). Lunch and afternoon snack are provided – freshly cooked, wholesome and organic.
We use the Berlin model: your child gets to know the group with a familiar parent or carer, and time apart grows step by step.

items.q: Where do the children play outside?
items.a: We don't have our own garden, but we go to Rubenspark, just a few minutes' walk away, every day – plus trips to the Prater or Wienerberg.

items.q: Do you prepare children for school?
items.a: Yes. In the compulsory kindergarten year there is a pre-school programme every Wednesday from 13:00 to 14:00, with extra activities during the week.
